mainTopic: Which details of a מנחה vow are binding, and the new משנה about vowing an improper מנחה (barley, lentils, partial measures), with the dispute between חזקיה and רבי יוחנן over why such a vow holds.
overview: The עמוד opens by finishing a rule from the previous עמוד. A person is bound to a specific type of מנחה only if he named it when he made his נדר, not if he named it later when he set aside the flour. The source is the פסוק 'כאשר נדרת', and רבי יוחנן taught the same rule. A new משנה then teaches that someone who vows an improper מנחה (from barley, from plain flour, without oil and לבונה, half a tenth or a tenth and a half) still brings a proper one, while רבי שמעון exempts him. The גמרא asks why a barley vow counts at all, since its own words seem to cancel it. חזקיה answers that the משנה follows בית שמאי, who go by the first words (תפוס לשון ראשון). רבי יוחנן answers that it can follow בית הלל too, when the person says he would have vowed properly had he known. חזקיה also limits the rule to barley and not lentils, and the גמרא explains that he dropped the בית שמאי reading: barley is an honest mistake people make, but lentils are not. Finally, רבי יוחנן's 'even from lentils' is explained as an argument against חזקיה. He shows that the משנה's choice of barley could be a 'לא מיבעיא' style, so חזקיה had no need to retract.

steps.title: The type only matters if it was fixed at the time of the vow
steps.stepSummary: This finishes the teaching (of אביי) that started on the previous עמוד. The משנה's rule that a switched מנחה does not fulfill the vow applies only when the type was named at the time of the נדר, not at the time of the הפרשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The משנה only taught this] when he fixed the type at the time of the vow. But if he fixed it at the time of setting aside the flour, it does not count.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a statement that limits the earlier משנה: a switched מנחה fails to fulfill the vow only if the type was named when he made the נדר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier משנה said that if someone vowed a מחבת and brought a מרחשת, what he brought counts as an offering, but he has not fulfilled his vow. This statement narrows that rule. It applies only when the type was part of the original נדר. If he simply vowed 'a מנחה' and named the type only later, when he set aside the flour, that later naming does not lock him in.

keyTerms.meaning: He fixed them, meaning he named the specific type of מנחה
At the time of the vow, when he first obligated himself
At the time of setting aside, when he designated the actual flour for his offering

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two moments. The נדר is the promise ('I will bring a מנחה'). The הפרשה is later, when he picks out the actual flour. Only what he said at the first moment is binding.

phrases.english: only when he fixed them at the time of the vow,
phrases.notes: This finishes a sentence from the previous עמוד that started 'they only taught' this rule of the משנה.

phrases.english: but at the time of setting aside, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues an אמורא's limitation of the previous משנה (from the prior עמוד).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only a type of מנחה named at the time of the נדר is binding. A type named at the הפרשה is not.

steps.title: The verse: 'according to what you vowed'
steps.stepSummary: The source for the rule: the פסוק says 'כאשר נדרת' (according to what you vowed), not 'according to what you set aside.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'according to what you vowed,' and not 'according to what you set aside.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the Torah source for the rule in step 1.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק ties the obligation to the words of the vow itself. Since the Torah did not say 'as you set aside,' anything added at the הפרשה is not part of the binding promise.

keyTerms.meaning: According to what you vowed (דברים 23:24)
You set aside or designated

phrases.english: "According to what you vowed,"
and not "according to what you set aside."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק behind the rule just stated.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that only a type fixed at the time of the נדר is binding.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן said the same thing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reports that רבי יוחנן (through רבי אסי and רבי אחא בר חנינא) taught exactly the same rule from the same פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also said: רבי אחא בר חנינא said in the name of רבי אסי, in the name of רבי יוחנן: The משנה only taught this when he fixed the type at the time of the vow. But at the time of setting aside, no, because the פסוק says 'according to what you vowed,' and not 'according to what you set aside.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the rule by showing that רבי יוחנן also taught it, word for word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new is added to the law. The point is that the rule is not a lone opinion: a major אמורא, רבי יוחנן, holds it too, with the same פסוק as his source.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught it when, a phrase that limits a משנה to a specific case

steps.whatToRemember: A vow is defined by its words at the moment of the נדר. Details added later, at the הפרשה, are not binding. The source is 'כאשר נדרת', and both חזקיה and רבי יוחנן hold this.

phrases.english: It was also stated:
Rabbi Aḥa bar Ḥanina said,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Asi said, Rabbi Yoḥanan said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁקְּבָעָן בִּשְׁעַת נֶדֶר,
phrases.english: They only taught this when he fixed them at the time of the vow,
but at the time of setting aside, no,
"according to what you vowed," and not "according to what you set aside."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the previous rule with the same teaching from רבי יוחנן.
steps.raayaSupportSource: An independent report of רבי יוחנן's teaching.

steps.title: New משנה: vowing a מנחה in a way that is not allowed
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה. Someone who vows a מנחה from barley brings wheat. Someone who vows one from plain flour brings סולת. Someone who vows one without oil and לבונה brings it with oil and לבונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who says 'I take upon myself a מנחה from barley' must bring one from wheat. If he said 'from plain flour,' he must bring fine flour (סולת). If he said 'without oil and without לבונה,' he must bring it with oil and לבונה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It deals with someone who vows a מנחה but adds a detail the Torah does not allow for a voluntary מנחה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A voluntary מנחה must be wheat, made of סולת, with oil and לבונה. When the vow includes an improper detail, the משנה says he still brings a proper מנחה. The basic vow to bring a מנחה stands, and the improper detail is not followed.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה, marking the start of a new משנה
Behold, it is upon me, the standard wording of a נדר
Barley
Plain, coarser flour
Fine flour, required for a מנחה
Frankincense, placed on a מנחה

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה does not say the vow is cancelled. He is still obligated, but he brings the offering in its proper form.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the coming גמרא discussion about what happens when a vow contains an impossible or improper detail.

phrases.english: MISHNA: One who says, "It is upon me to bring a meal offering
from barley," should bring it from wheat.
"Flour": he should bring fine flour.
"Without oil and without frankincense":
he should bring oil and frankincense.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הָאוֹמֵר הֲרֵי עָלַי מִנְחָה מִן הַשְּׂעוֹרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה with a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A vow for an improper מנחה (barley, plain flour, or without oil and לבונה) still obligates him, and he brings a proper one (wheat, סולת, with oil and לבונה).

steps.title: Vowing half a tenth or a tenth and a half
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues. A vow of half an עשרון requires a full עשרון, and a vow of one and a half requires two. רבי שמעון exempts him in all these cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone says 'half a tenth,' he brings a whole tenth. If he says 'a tenth and a half,' he brings two tenths. רבי שמעון says he does not have to bring anything, because he did not vow the way people normally vow.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה from the previous step keeps going with more cases where someone vows a מנחה in a form that is not normally brought.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The smallest מנחה is one עשרון, and there are no partial tenths. So the תנא קמא rounds the vow up to the next whole number. רבי שמעון disagrees: a vow that does not fit any real offering simply does not take effect.

keyTerms.meaning: A tenth of an איפה, the basic measure of flour for a מנחה
Exempts; says he owes nothing
In the way people normally pledge

steps.whatToRemember: The תנא קמא makes him bring a proper version of what he vowed. רבי שמעון says a vow that is not 'the way people vow' does not take effect at all.

phrases.english: If he vowed 'half a tenth', he brings a complete tenth;
if he vowed 'a tenth and a half', he brings two tenths.
Rabbi Shimon exempts him,
because he did not pledge in the way people pledge.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה begun in step 4 with more cases of odd vows
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Half a tenth means bring one tenth, and a tenth and a half means bring two. רבי שמעון exempts in all these cases because the vow was not made the normal way.

steps.title: Why does a barley vow count at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה makes someone who vowed a barley מנחה bring wheat. His own words seem to undo the vow.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why? This is a vow that comes with its own way out!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by challenging the תנא קמא of the משנה. Why should a vow like 'a מנחה from barley' obligate him at all?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'I will bring a מנחה' creates a vow. Adding 'from barley' seems to cancel it, because a regular מנחה cannot be barley. A vow that carries its own cancellation inside it should not take effect, so why must he bring wheat?

keyTerms.meaning: Why?
A vow with its 'opening' (its way out) built in. The vow is undone by its own words.

steps.confusionAlert: The 'why' refers back to the barley case at the start of the משנה (step 4), not to the half-tenth case just mentioned.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Why?
phrases.notes: He is asking about the first case of the משנה: someone who vowed barley has to bring wheat.

phrases.english: It is a vow with its own opening right alongside it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of the משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that one who vows a barley מנחה must bring wheat
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The second part of his words ('from barley') contradicts and cancels the first part, so there should be no vow at all.

steps.title: חזקיה: The משנה follows בית שמאי
steps.stepSummary: חזקיה answers that the משנה follows בית שמאי, who say we go by the first thing a person said.
steps.simpleTranslation: חזקיה said: Whose view is this? It is בית שמאי, who say: hold on to the first words.
steps.whatsHappening: חזקיה answers the question by saying this משנה follows only בית שמאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For בית שמאי, once he says 'I will bring a מנחה' the vow is already in place. The words that come after cannot cancel it. So 'from barley' is ignored, and he must bring a normal wheat מנחה.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose view is this?
Hold on to the first words; the later words don't cancel them

phrases.english: Ḥizkiyya said: Whose view is this?
It is Beit Shammai,
who say: hold on to the first statement.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributes the משנה to one side of a מחלוקת (בית שמאי)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed the משנה follows everyone, so its words should cancel the vow.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה follows בית שמאי, who go by the first words. The vow stands and the barley part is ignored.

steps.title: The proof: the נזיר from dried figs
steps.stepSummary: חזקיה shows where בית שמאי hold this, using a משנה about a man who says he is a נזיר from figs.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: 'I am a נזיר from dried figs and pressed figs.' בית שמאי say he is a נזיר. בית הלל say he is not a נזיר.
steps.whatsHappening: This backs up חזקיה's answer with a משנה where בית שמאי and בית הלל argue about the same kind of mixed-up statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Figs are not forbidden to a נזיר, so 'from figs' contradicts 'I am a נזיר'. בית שמאי go by the first words and make him a full נזיר. בית הלל let the second part undo the first. That is why חזקיה can only fit our משנה with בית שמאי.

keyTerms.meaning: A person who has vowed not to drink wine, cut his hair, or become טמא from a dead body
Dried figs
Pressed fig cake

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that חזקיה's answer has a cost: it means our משנה does not follow בית הלל, and normally the הלכה follows בית הלל. That sets up רבי יוחנן's different answer.

phrases.english: As we learned: 'I am hereby a nazirite'
'from dried figs and from pressed figs' —
Beit Shammai say: he is a nazirite;
and Beit Hillel say: he is not a nazirite.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן הֲרֵינִי נָזִיר מִן הַגְּרוֹגְרוֹת וּמִן הַדְּבֵילָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the view of בית שמאי that חזקיה relied on
steps.raayaObject: That בית שמאי hold 'go by the first words' and בית הלל do not
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in נזיר 9a about the נזיר from dried figs

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: Even בית הלל agree in this case
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the משנה can follow בית הלל too. It speaks of someone who says he would have vowed the right way had he known.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: You can even say it is בית הלל. The case is where he says: 'If I had known that people don't vow this way, I would not have vowed this way, but that way.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a second answer to the question in step 6, so that the משנה does not have to follow only בית שמאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the second words are not meant to undo the vow. They were only a mistake about how a מנחה is brought. Once he says he really meant to vow a proper מנחה, even בית הלל agree that the vow stands and he brings wheat.

keyTerms.meaning: You can even say (the משנה fits this view too)
If I had known

steps.whatToRemember: Two answers: חזקיה says the משנה follows בית שמאי (go by the first words). רבי יוחנן says it fits בית הלל too, when the person shows he really wanted a proper מנחה.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא בֵּית הִלֵּל,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said: You can even say it is Beit Hillel,
where he says: 'Had I known
that one does not vow like this,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא הָיִיתִי נוֹדֵר כָּךְ אֶלָּא כָּךְ״.
phrases.english: I would not have vowed like this, but like that.'
phrases.notes: 'Like that' means the proper way: a מנחה of wheat.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא בֵּית הִלֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer to the step 6 challenge instead of חזקיה's answer
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrows the case of the משנה (a specific kind of speaker)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Per חזקיה, the משנה can only follow בית שמאי.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה fits בית הלל too. It speaks of someone who says he would have vowed a proper מנחה had he known, so his words never cancelled the vow.

steps.title: Barley works, lentils do not
steps.stepSummary: חזקיה says the משנה's rule applies only when someone said barley. If he said lentils, the vow does not take effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: חזקיה said: The משנה only taught this when he said 'a מנחה from barley.' But if he said 'a מנחה from lentils,' the rule does not apply.
steps.whatsHappening: חזקיה gives a new statement that narrows the משנה: the rule that he brings wheat applies only to a vow mentioning barley, not lentils.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said someone who vows a barley מנחה must bring wheat. חזקיה adds a limit. If the person said lentils, we do not make him bring anything.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this case; it limits the rule
Flour offering, normally brought from wheat
Barley
Lentils

phrases.english: Ḥizkiyya said:
They taught it only
phrases.notes: He means the משנה's rule that the person must bring a wheat מנחה.

phrases.english: where he said: 'A meal offering from barley,'
but if he said: 'A meal offering from lentils,' then no.
phrases.notes: 'No' means the vow does not take effect at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a new limit by חזקיה on the משנה's barley case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A vow of a barley מנחה obligates wheat. A vow of a lentil מנחה is not binding.

steps.title: Why should lentils be different?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that חזקיה said the משנה follows בית שמאי, who go by the first words. Under that view, barley and lentils should be the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, according to whom did חזקיה explain his teaching? According to בית שמאי. And בית שמאי rule this way because we hold on to the first words a person said. So what difference does it make to me whether he said barley or lentils?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges חזקיה using his own earlier explanation from Step 7.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under תפוס לשון ראשון, only the words 'a מנחה' count, and whatever he said afterward is ignored. So it should not matter whether the ignored words were barley or lentils. Treating them differently clashes with חזקיה's own reasoning.

keyTerms.meaning: Now, after all; opens a reasoning that leads to a challenge
A teaching or ruling a sage holds
Hold on to the first words; later words do not cancel them
What difference does it make to me? There should be no difference

phrases.english: Now, according to whom did Ḥizkiyya say his teaching?
phrases.notes: This points back to Step 7, where חזקיה said the משנה follows בית שמאי.

phrases.english: According to Beit Shammai,

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵית שַׁמַּאי מִשּׁוּם תְּפוֹס לָשׁוֹן רִאשׁוֹן הוּא.
phrases.english: and Beit Shammai's reason is: hold on to the first words.
What difference is it to me whether from barley
or from lentils?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks Step 10 using חזקיה's own reasoning from Step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: חזקיה's distinction between barley and lentils
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the first words are all that count, the later words, whether barley or lentils, are equally ignored, so there is no basis for a difference.

steps.title: חזקיה changed his mind
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that חזקיה took back his earlier explanation that the משנה follows בית שמאי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by saying חזקיה dropped his earlier view that the משנה follows בית שמאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two statements do not clash, because the barley-and-lentils statement came after he gave up the בית שמאי explanation. So it is no longer built on תפוס לשון ראשון.

keyTerms.meaning: He went back on it; he changed his mind

steps.confusionAlert: חזקיה is not changing the barley-and-lentils rule. He is changing his earlier explanation from Step 7, that the משנה follows בית שמאי.

phrases.english: He retracted.
phrases.notes: He took back his Step 7 explanation that the משנה follows בית שמאי.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Retraction: the earlier premise is dropped
steps.terutzHavaAmina: חזקיה still holds the משנה follows בית שמאי, so barley and lentils should be the same.
steps.terutzMaskana: חזקיה gave up the בית שמאי explanation, so his distinction stands.

steps.title: Why did he change his mind?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what made חזקיה drop his בית שמאי explanation.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the reason he retracted?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question to set up the next step, which will explain why חזקיה changed his mind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A sage does not drop a view for no reason. The גמרא wants to find what in the משנה pushed him away from the בית שמאי reading.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: And what is the reason he retracted?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the answer in Step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What led חזקיה to drop his בית שמאי explanation.

steps.title: The משנה's choice of barley bothered him
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the wording of the משנה troubled חזקיה. If the משנה followed בית שמאי, it should have used the bigger case of lentils.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The משנה was hard for him. Why does it specifically teach 'a מנחה from barley'? Let it teach 'from lentils'!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question by showing the problem חזקיה found in the משנה's wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under בית שמאי, any later words are ignored. Then the most impressive example would be lentils, which are even further from a real מנחה. Since the משנה chose barley instead, it looks like barley is special.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
It was difficult for him
Why specifically this case?
Let it teach

phrases.english: Rava said:
The mishna was difficult for him:
Why does it specifically teach 'a meal offering from barley'?
Let it teach 'from lentils'!

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה's choice of barley over lentils did not fit the בית שמאי reading.

steps.title: The real reason is a mistake
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the vow holds because the person made a mistake. People can make that mistake about barley, but not about lentils.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, learn from this: the reason is because he made a mistake. With barley a person can make a mistake. With lentils he does not make a mistake.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the conclusion that explains both חזקיה's change of mind and his barley-and-lentils rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The vow holds with barley because someone could honestly think a מנחה may come from barley. That fits the idea in Step 9 of a person who would have vowed correctly had he known. Nobody thinks a מנחה comes from lentils, so saying lentils shows he never meant a real vow.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; introduces the corrected understanding
Learn from it; a conclusion drawn
He makes a mistake

steps.whatToRemember: חזקיה dropped the בית שמאי reading. The barley vow holds because it is an honest mistake. Lentils are not a believable mistake, so that vow does not hold.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the reason a vow holds decides how far it reaches. A rule based on honest mistakes covers only mistakes people really make.

phrases.english: Rather, learn from this:
it is because he makes a mistake.
With barley, he can make a mistake,
with lentils, he does not make a mistake.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from רבא's point in Step 14.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה is not based on תפוס לשון ראשון but on an honest mistake. That is why barley obligates him and lentils do not.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: Even a vow from lentils takes effect
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says that the vow to bring a מנחה takes effect even if the person said 'from lentils.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: Even if he vowed to bring it from lentils, the vow takes effect.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives רבי יוחנן's side of the dispute with חזקיה from step 10. He says that even a person who vows a מנחה 'from lentils' must bring a proper מנחה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Barley is at least used for some offerings, but lentils are never used for any מנחה. רבי יוחנן is saying the vow takes effect even in this more extreme case. The next step will ask how this fits with his own explanation of the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Lentils, which are never used for any מנחה
A flour offering, normally brought from wheat

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
Even from lentils.
phrases.notes: He means that even if someone vowed a מנחה 'from lentils,' the vow still holds and he brings a regular one.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ מִן הָעֲדָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי יוחנן's side of the dispute with חזקיה's statement in step 10 (barley only, not lentils). Steps 11–15 were a side discussion of חזקיה's view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A vow to bring a מנחה from lentils also takes effect.

steps.title: How can רבי יוחנן include lentils if he follows בית הלל?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains the משנה like בית הלל, who rely on the person's mistake. People mistake barley for a valid מנחה, but not lentils.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, whose opinion does רבי יוחנן follow in his explanation? בית הלל's. And בית הלל say the vow holds because the person made a mistake. With barley, he could make that mistake. With lentils, he would not!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's statement and says it does not fit with his own approach to the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to בית הלל, the vow works only because we assume the person honestly made a mistake. That makes sense for barley, which people might think works for a מנחה. Nobody thinks lentils work, so under בית הלל a lentil vow should not take effect.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Now, after all,' an opening word that sets up a logical challenge
His teaching, here meaning his explanation of the משנה
He makes a mistake

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two views. בית שמאי go by the first words a person says. בית הלל go by the idea that the person made a mistake. Only the mistake idea separates barley from lentils.

phrases.english: Now, Rabbi Yoḥanan,
in accordance with whom did he say his teaching?
In accordance with Beit Hillel,
and Beit Hillel say it is because he made a mistake.
With barley, he makes that mistake;
with lentils, he does not make that mistake!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּדֵי, רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן כְּמַאן אַמְרַהּ לִשְׁמַעְתֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling stated in step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's claim that a vow from lentils takes effect
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן's בית הלל approach depends on the person making a mistake. That mistake is possible with barley but not with lentils, so the lentil case should not work.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן was arguing on חזקיה's own terms
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן was not stating his own view. He was responding to חזקיה and asking why חזקיה gave up his בית שמאי explanation.
steps.simpleTranslation: He was speaking to חזקיה according to חזקיה's own words: 'Why did you take back your explanation? Because the משנה does not say "from lentils"?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יוחנן was not giving his own ruling. He was challenging חזקיה. This step sets up the argument that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן himself agrees that lentils do not work under בית הלל. His 'even from lentils' really belongs to חזקיה's original בית שמאי approach, where the first words count, so lentils would work too. He is questioning חזקיה's reason for dropping that approach.

keyTerms.meaning: According to his words, meaning arguing from the other person's position
He took back what he said

phrases.english: He was speaking to him according to the words of Ḥizkiyya:
You, what is the reason you took back your view?
Because the mishna does not teach "from lentils."
phrases.notes: This points back to step 14, where רבא explained that the missing lentil case is what made חזקיה change his mind.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 17 by reframing רבי יוחנן's statement as an argument against חזקיה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reframing: the statement was made on the other person's terms, not as the speaker's own ruling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought רבי יוחנן personally held that lentils work, which clashes with בית הלל.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוחנן was only saying that under חזקיה's בית שמאי approach, lentils would work, and that חזקיה had no good reason to drop it.

steps.title: The משנה may use a 'not only this, but even that' style
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rejects חזקיה's reason for retracting. The משנה may be teaching the bigger point: lentils obviously work, and even barley, where a mistake is possible, also works by the first words.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps the משנה is speaking in a 'no need to say' style. There is no need to say the vow works with lentils, where we could say he took back his words and we hold onto the first words. Even with barley, where we could say he simply made a mistake, we still hold onto the first words.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן shows that the משנה can still follow בית שמאי even though it mentions barley and not lentils. So חזקיה had no need to take back his explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With lentils, the person knowingly said something invalid, which looks like going back on his words, and בית שמאי ignore that. Barley is actually the harder case for בית שמאי, because there the person may have honestly made a mistake. So mentioning barley is the bigger new point, and the משנה's choice of barley is no proof against בית שמאי.

keyTerms.meaning: 'No need to say,' a style that teaches the harder case and leaves the easier case understood
Hold onto the first words a person said, the rule of בית שמאי
Making an honest mistake

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's 'even from lentils' fits only חזקיה's בית שמאי approach. Under בית שמאי, barley is the bigger point, because an honest mistake might seem to cancel the vow. Even so, the first words still hold.
steps.confusionAlert: Under בית הלל, lentils are the harder case. Under בית שמאי, barley is the harder case. Which case counts as the 'bigger point' depends on which view you are following.
steps.whyThisMatters: This step shows that a משנה's choice of example does not always prove which opinion it follows, because the 'לא מיבעיא' style can flip which case counts as the bigger point.

phrases.english: Perhaps it is speaking in a "no need to say" style:
There is no need to say from lentils,
where one can say
that he simply took back his words,
and we hold onto the first words;
but even from barley as well,
where one can say
that he honestly made a mistake,
even so, we hold onto the first words.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי יוחנן's challenge to חזקיה that was set up in step 18.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects חזקיה's reason for dropping the בית שמאי explanation, which רבא gave in step 14
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The missing lentil case proves nothing. Under בית שמאי, barley is the bigger point, so the משנה may be using a 'לא מיבעיא' style.
